content.text: This trace shows route-plan's server span at 16 s with only 1.2 s in its client calls, so route-plan's own work or an unseen callee is involved. I'll measure self-time for the slow methods inside travel2 and route-plan, using child durations.

input.query: WITH c AS (SELECT parent_span_id pid, sum(duration) cd, count(*) nc FROM abnormal_traces GROUP BY 1) SELECT s.service_name, s.attr_span_kind, left(s.span_name,60) sn, count(*) n, round(quantile_cont(s.duration,0.5)/1e6,1) dur_p50, round(quantile_cont(s.duration - coalesce(c.cd,0),0.5)/1e6,1) self_p50, round(avg(s.duration - coalesce(c.cd,0))/1e6,1) self_avg, round(avg(coalesce(c.nc,0)),1) avg_children FROM abnormal_traces s LEFT JOIN c ON c.pid = s.span_id WHERE s.service_name IN ('ts-travel2-service','ts-route-plan-service','ts-travel-plan-service') AND s.duration > 500000000 GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 1,2,3

content.text: The travel2 slowness is in-process: getRouteByTripId and queryInfo spend about 3.6 s and 10.9 s in their own bodies, while their children are only a few ms. Route-plan and travel-plan are slow only because they wait on travel2. Next I'll check whether the mild rises in other services come from MySQL, which the survey flagged with a CPU shift.
